newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's king calls for clean up of cities.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's king calls for clean up of cities.

text.p: Morocco's King Hassan has called for an urgent cleanup of the country's dirty cities, the official MAP news agency said on Thursday.

MAP quoted the king as saying in a letter to Interior Minister Driss Basri that "urgent and efficient measures should be taken to safeguard the cleanliness of the kingdom's cities and their environment."
"Signs of negligence appeared...and represented a threat to the citizen's health and disturb the quietude of inhabitants and visitors," he added.

Earlier this year the environment ministry said pollution was costing 20 billion dirhams ($2.3 billion) a year "but could largely be beaten by spending 4.6 billion dirhams a year which would bring annual economic benefits of 14.2 billion dirhams."
Waste, rubbish and pollution threaten beaches which should be a magnet for the average three million tourists visiting Morocco each year, officials said.
